query: How can we reduce declined travel expenses?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: The type of asset/expense is not something an actor sets to reduce declines, but it plausibly affects both what documentation/method is used and whether the expense is declined; a pre-existing attribute of the expense acting as a common cause.

per_column.name: travel_expense_relevance
per_column.rationale: This essentially flags whether a row is a travel expense at all -- it is a scoping/selection variable implied by the query focus, not a treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: expense_initiation_method
per_column.rationale: Automated vs manual submission is an intervenable, configurable process lever an organization could set/change to affect decline rates.

per_column.name: documentation_completeness
per_column.rationale: Whether the submission includes complete documentation (source_id) is an actionable lever -- policy/enforcement could require complete docs to reduce declines.

per_column.name: asset_cost_tier_signal
per_column.rationale: Cost tier plausibly influences both scrutiny/method of processing and the likelihood of decline; a pre-existing common cause not settable as an intervention.

per_column.name: processing_delay_presence
per_column.rationale: Processing delay likely lies on the causal path between submission method/documentation and the decline outcome rather than being a common cause; treated as a mediator, not a confounder.

per_column.name: requestor_department
per_column.rationale: Department is already present in the original table and clearly implied; it can affect both submission practices (method/docs) and decline rates, so a confounder, but named in query context.

per_column.name: requestor_frequency_pattern
per_column.rationale: How often a requestor submits plausibly affects both their submission behavior/method and their decline likelihood (familiarity), acting as a common cause; largely a fixed behavioral attribute rather than a direct lever.

judge.rationale: The set genuinely realizes the what-if claim: it includes at least two intervenable treatments (expense_initiation_method and documentation_completeness) that an actor could set or enforce to reduce declines, satisfying part (a). For part (b), several plausible confounders NOT named in the query are supplied (asset_category_type, asset_cost_tier_signal, requestor_frequency_pattern) that are common causes of both submission practices and decline likelihood, demonstrating the capability under test. However, confounder quality is only moderate: processing_delay_presence is really a mediator (should be excluded from adjustment), requestor_department is already implied by the original schema, and travel_expense_relevance is a scoping flag. The confounders adjust for asset/cost/behavior common causes but leave the treatment-outcome identification only partially secured.
